observation.visible_scene: A low sun (sunrise or sunset) sits right of center in a layered cloud-filled sky, above a dark silhouetted hillside and tree line in the foreground with faint distant hills on the right. A small cyan lens-flare dot is visible in the upper-middle sky during the brighter portions. The clip runs at near real-time (frames ~0.067 s apart).
visible_changes: The sun's apparent position in the sky stays roughly fixed (center-right, similar height in first and last frames); its brightness, not its location, changes.

A long dark horizontal cloud band drifts across the sun, progressively occluding it: the sun is a bright open disk in early frames, is largely hidden behind the cloud (only a diffuse glow) around the middle frames, then re-emerges as a smaller bright disk, and is again partly covered by a thin cloud sliver near the end.
As the sun is covered and uncovered, the surrounding sky alternates between warm golden illumination and cooler, muted purple-grey tones.
The cyan lens-flare dot is present while the sun is bright (early frames), fades when the sun is occluded, and faintly reappears when the sun brightens again.

Upper and side clouds translate slowly and deform (edges shifting) across the sky; the foreground tree silhouette shows small, irregular branch movements consistent with wind rather than camera motion.
The overall framing of the horizon and trees shifts only slightly, indicating little or no deliberate camera pan/zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the sun is rising or setting, and its trajectory before/after this 2.7 s excerpt.
The full duration and pacing of the cloud movement beyond the crop boundaries.
The cause of the cloud drift and any camera intent.
uncertain_details: Exact camera behavior: the background evidence is insufficient to distinguish a fixed tripod shot from slight handheld drift.
Whether the small foreground branch changes are wind sway or compression artifacts.
Precise timing of each occlusion/reveal event relative to real-world cloud motion.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
